correctness.rationale: The exact gain for protecting leaf i is G_i=sum over edges e containing i of length(e)*Pr(C_e subset E), with no independence assumption. Full-root clades add a common constant to all gains, proving the n<=k+1 sufficiency even with a root stem. For n=k+2, the signed binomial finite-difference perturbation annihilates factorial moments through n-2 and keeps mass at n fixed, but shifts q_(n-1) by 2epsilon/n. The clade A versus singleton d tree makes d and a exchange unique best positions; positivity and strict separation persist for sufficiently small positive delta. Independent exact enumeration of all 16 extinction subsets in the four-taxon witness gives gains (43/16,5/4,1,11/4) and (45/16,11/8,9/8,11/4). Finite n<=10 tests are not used as proof of all k.
